evals.prompt: Run a read-only security assessment of my Amazon SageMaker setup in us-east-1 and give me a severity-rated findings report.
evals.expected_output: A structured, severity-rated Amazon SageMaker security findings report organized by Check_ID (SM-01..SM-25), each finding carrying a status (Passed, Failed, or N/A), a severity, and a verifiability classification. The assessment is strictly read-only. When no SageMaker resources exist in the account/region, the relevant checks are reported N/A rather than Passed, and any control that cannot be read is never marked Passed.
assertions: The report classifies each finding's Verifiability as one of Verifiable, Heuristic, or Prescribe-only
Findings are identified by SageMaker check IDs and each carries a severity and a status
Controls that cannot be read or do not apply are reported as N/A rather than Passed

assertions.text: The report references SageMaker check IDs in the SM-NN form
The response describes the assessment as read-only

assertions: The response states it only calls read-only Describe/List/Get operations and does not modify any resource
Checks for which no SageMaker resources exist in the account/region are reported as N/A rather than Passed

evals.prompt: According to the skill, what are the three verifiability classifications for a check, and how must the report treat each with respect to a Passed status? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Names Verifiable, Heuristic, and Prescribe-only. Verifiable: Passed/Failed/N/A from returned data. Heuristic: cite evidence, N/A (not Passed) when ambiguous or denied. Prescribe-only: always N/A, never Passed/Failed.
assertions: Explains that a Prescribe-only check is always reported N/A and is never marked Passed or Failed

evals.prompt: For check SM-02 (SageMaker IAM permissions), which aspects are Prescribe-only and must never be marked Passed, and why? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: The stale-access aspect (needs iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails, a Generate* verb blocked by the read-only guardrail) and the IAM Identity Center configuration aspect (not control-plane readable) are Prescribe-only and always N/A; only the AmazonSageMakerFullAccess detection is Heuristic.
assertions: Identifies the stale SageMaker access aspect as Prescribe-only because it needs iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails, a blocked Generate* verb

assertions.text: Mentions the IAM Identity Center aspect

assertions: States that the IAM Identity Center configuration aspect is not readable from the control plane and is therefore reported N/A

evals.prompt: What does this skill defer to aiml-access-diagnostics, and does it call the AWS Security Hub API? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Defers reactive diagnosis of a specific access denial (authorization-chain tracing) to aiml-access-diagnostics; it reports static posture only. It cites Security Hub control IDs (SageMaker.1-5) for cross-reference but does not call securityhub:* APIs.
assertions: Explains that diagnosing why a specific SageMaker call was denied is deferred to the aiml-access-diagnostics skill, and that this skill reports static posture only

assertions.text: Cites the Security Hub control IDs SageMaker.1 to 5 as cross-references
States that Security Hub is cross-referenced, not called

evals.prompt: Is this a read-only assessment and what verbs may it call? Can it remediate findings automatically? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Strictly read-only: only Describe*/List*/Get*/BatchGet*; never creates, modifies, deletes, enables, or disables anything, and never calls Generate* verbs. It does not remediate; it reports guidance only.

assertions.text: Names the read-only verb families it may call

assertions: Explains that remediation is reported as guidance only and that the assessment never modifies, creates, or deletes resources itself

evals.prompt: According to the skill, when does check SM-15 (Feature Store encryption) fail versus pass? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: SM-15 fails when a feature group offline store lacks a KmsKeyId, passes when all offline stores use a customer-managed KMS key, and is N/A when no feature groups with offline stores exist.
assertions: States that SM-15 fails when a feature group offline store lacks a KmsKeyId, and passes only when all offline stores use a customer-managed KMS key

evals.prompt: What fields must each finding contain and what pattern must Check_ID match? Name the allowed Status values. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Fields: Check_ID, Finding, Finding_Details, Resolution, Reference, Severity, Status, Verifiability, Region (and optional Account). Check_ID matches ^SM-\d{2}$. Status is one of Failed, Passed, N/A.
assertions: Specifies that Check_ID must match the pattern SM- followed by two digits (for example SM-01)
